Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

As expected, Alonso tasked his players with deploying a possession-based strategy in which the ball is worked from back to front between the lines. At times, Alonso’s vision was executed in style: Chelsea’s two goals in the first half were both the consequence of slick passing moves.

There were plenty of other occasions, though, when Chelsea were sloppy in their passing and defensively exposed when they lost the ball. The best example of this was in the second half, when Estêvão’s error allowed Western Sydney Wanderers to score their fourth goal of the game.

Admittedly, Chelsea’s attempts to play passing football were not helped by the poor quality of the pitch in Sydney. A recent rugby game had created a bobbly, unpredictable surface which caused no end of problems for Chelsea’s midfield players. That may sound like an excuse for their sloppiness, but it is probably a fair one.

Chelsea started the game with two Reggies in their midfield. Reggie Walsh is a 17-year-old technician who last year became the club’s third-youngest player, and was loved by former head coach Enzo Maresca. He played as the No 10.

Reggie Watson, meanwhile, is the son of former Premier League midfielder Ben and is one of the most exciting talents in English football. A composed central midfielder, Watson is a regular for England’s youth teams and is the youngest player on Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

Both players showed glimpses of their talent in this match in Sydney. Watson was trusted with set-piece duties and produced some excellent deliveries, while also playing some lovely passes through the lines. Watson was the only Chelsea player to feature for the full 90 minutes, which spoke volumes of the quality of his performance.

Walsh was less involved but caught the eye in a couple of moments, not least when playing a delicate one-two with Essugo in advance of the midfielder’s first-half strike.

Satpayev is technically not a Chelsea player yet, as his deal officially commences when he turns 18 in August. His former club, Kairat, gave special dispensation to allow the teenager to join Chelsea’s pre-season tour ahead of the completion of his £3m transfer, which means he is officially in Australia as a “triallist”.

Satpayev is a player of obvious talent and has already played nine games for Kazakhstan. Before this move to Chelsea, he scored 21 goals in 41 games in the Kazakhstan Premier League.

The first sighting of Satpayev was an exciting one for Chelsea supporters, who saw the new man’s running speed and shooting power as he scored the opening goal of the game. Running in behind the Western Sydney Wanderers defence, Satpayev surged clear of the opposition and launched a scorching shot into the roof of the net.

Gittens endured a hugely disappointing first campaign at Chelsea last season, following his £52m move from Borussia Dortmund. Injury issues did not help his cause but he struggled to make much of an impact when he was fully fit, scoring just one goal in 27 appearances in all competitions.

Gittens is therefore a man with it all to prove at Stamford Bridge this season, and he has started the new campaign in promising form. His goal here came after two strikes in two behind-closed-doors friendly games before Chelsea left for Australia. Gittens was a constant threat after coming onto the pitch in the 63rd minute, showing his pace on the wing and his ability to go down the touchline or cut inside. His challenge now is to replicate this level of performance against better opposition.

A late revival ensures Chelsea win their first pre-season friendly under Xabi Alonso. There was a step up in class once Palmer, Pedro, Gittens, Estevao and Palestra were introduced, and the Australian side could not contain them. No injuries on a dogy pitching probably the biggest victory for the new manager.

Just the three minutes of added time to play.

Three goals in nine minutes for the Brazilian. Excellent corner delivery from Estevao, Fofana’s header blocked but then Joao Pedro turns home from close range. Baffling decision by Brazil not to take him to the World Cup.

Chelsea flooding forward again, and they have a corner in the last minute of normal time.

Chelsea now lead 5-4, Cole Palmer picking out Joao Pedro with the through ball but Western Sydney Wanderers were far too open. Joao Pedro shows his composure, sitting the defender down and rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

Estevao shows he has not lost his burst of speed after that serious hamstring injury but his shot flies straight into the side netting. Joao Pedro then delights the crowd with another piece of skill.

Jamie Gittens is having a good pre-season, having scored in two behind-closed-doors friendlies before this game in Australia. He has looked sharp since coming off the bench and has been involved in two of Chelsea’s goals.

Gittens had a disappointing first season at Chelsea following his £52m move from Dortmund last summer and is clearly keen to impress Alonso.

Robert Sanchez picks out Gittens with a raking pass, but his shot is blocked. The same is true for Joao Pedro’s follow up attempt. Gittens has impressed since coming on.

Poor defensive header back into a dangerous area from Gittens’s cross, but it is a crisp touch and finish from Joao Pedro, picking out the bottom corner. Chelsea level at 4-4. The move started with a quick free-kick, from Palmer, which he won.

Western Sydney Wanderers score their fourth goal of the game. Chelsea make another error when playing out from the back, it was Estevao who sold Reggie Watson short. One pass and one shot later, Awan Lual finishes beyond Sanchez.

Mazy run inside from Estevao off the right flank, but there was not quite enough power in his shot to beat the goalkeeper.

Joao Pedro is very good at taking the ball in and making it stick. Palestra looks very progressive from right-back, looks full of running and attacking intent.

Some of Western Sydney Wanderers’s corner routines have been quite nifty, Chelsea opened up from a short one again. Palmer with a velvety touch in midield and pass forward towards Palestra who was breaking forward.

Gittens scores, and the introduction of the senior players has made a difference already. Levi Colwill started the move with a longer pass forward, before Joao Pedro skips through challenges to tee up Gittens.

Nine changes made by Alonso: Palmer, Estevao, Palestra, Gittens, Sanchez, Colwill, Anselmino, Joao Pedro and Fofana are the players who have come on.

The Australian side now lead. Emenalo’s clearance deflects off a Western Sydney Wanderers player, and falls kindly to Scicluna, who drills his show beyond Sharman-Lowe into the bottom corner. He come the Chelsea changes.

Western Sydney Wanderers playing some good football in the last few minutes, Saptaev outmuscled in midfield and a shot comes in from the edge of the area. Sharman-Lowe saves, then Tosin clears after a short corner routine.

This young Chelsea side, which is still dealing with jet lag, looks a little tired now. They have not been under huge pressure but they can hardly complain about falling 3-2 behind. Here come all the big names, as Alonso makes huge changes for the last 30 minutes.

Chelsea enjoying a spell of comfortable possession, the tempo of the game has dropped. Good play again, from Reggie Watson, finding Emenalo on the overlap but he slices his shot high and wide when there was time to take aim.

Chelsea remain committed to passing out from the back, but the uneven pitch is making that difficult. Sharman-Lowe passes the ball straight out for a throw-in. Good defending from Acheampong to deal with a teasing cross.

Chelsea win a free-kick in a shooting position, and Reggie Watson takes it with his right foot. He goes goalkeeper’s side but, it shot curls just wide of the post.

Western Sydney Wanderers kick off in the second half.

Kellyman on for Essugo in midfield, and Nicoll-Jazuli replaces Kavuma-McQueen.

Some eye-catching football from Chelsea going forward, but some loose defending too. Suspect it is not long before we see Palmer, Estevao, Colwill and Joao Pedro. Walsh and Watson have done well in midfield for Chelsea.

Half-time! 🕰️Watch the second half LIVE on CFC+ 📺

Another really bad miss from Tosin. Free header from a corner, could see it all the way, but he skewed the ball wide from a just a couple of yards out. Chelsea should be in front.

Subuloye wins a back post header from the Chelsea corner, but the “home” team clear. More goals in this game, surely. Saptaev wins Chelsea a corner with another burst forward.

This is a great team goal. Essugo started the move, finding Saptaev down the left. Essugo moves the ball on two Walsh, who gives it him back with a slick one-two and Essugo rolls the ball into the bottom corner.

That’s the second impressive team goal that Chelsea have scored in this first half. Essugo to Walsh, Walsh to Essugo, Essugo finds the corner. Walsh, 17, has produced some nice touches in the No 10 position. Last year he became the third-youngest player in Chelsea’s history and you can see he is a supremely talented teenager.

Chelsea in trouble defensively again, passing their way into trouble on the edge of their defensive third. I’m sure there will be a raft of half-time changes, but that was probably the plan all along.

Chelsea have been alarmingly open and easy to play through. The collective structure and individual defending were both poor in advance of that second Western Sydney Wanderers goal. I expect they’ll tighten up when the more experienced players come into the game.

Hammond is the goalscorer, and it is a finish of genuine quality. Silky touch to flick the ball inside Josh Acheampong, and fire low into the bottom corner. Soft Chelsea defending, though.

Smooth combination play from Walsh and Watson, the two Reggies in Chelsea’s midfield, before Saptaev shoots over the bar form the edge of the box. A shame for marketing people and headline writers that one of Walsh or Watson are not called Ronnie.

Reggie Watson with a foul in midfield. Fair to say Chelsea’s youthful team are on the back foot now, but there was nice turn in midfield from Essugo after more passing out from the back. Clear that is an emphasis for Alonso.

Sharman-Lowe claims a cross, but Western Sydney Wanderers down their right flank again. I almost anticipated a hydration break at this stage, but it is back to business as usual. Chelsea flagging a touch after a lively start.

Chelsea’s defence looking a touch exposed again, but Borrello curls a shot wide of the post. Emenalo has down well going forward but there was space down his side there.

Two causes for concern for Chelsea in the first 15 minutes here. The first is the pitch in Sydney, which looks terrible. The ball is bobbling all over midfield, making it very difficult for Chelsea’s central players in particular. The second concern will be their defending for that set-piece, as Western Sydney Wanderers had two free headers.

Liam Delap has not been particularly involved, but Reggie Watson almost found him with a cute reverse pass. Watson the plays a progressive pass forward from deep.

Reggie Walsh pushes forward and takes on a shot from long range. Well struck, another save from the goalkeeper. From the resulting corner, taken by Watson, Tosin misses a free header. Good chance, should have hit the target.

Chelsea concede from the corner. Flicked on at the near post and a free header at the back stick for Anthony Pantazopoulos. One for Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’ new set-piece coach, to clip up and show in the team meeting.

Emenalo fouled after more neat football out from the back by Chelsea. Alonso is on his feet on the touchline, barking instructions. Emenalo has showed some silky touches.

Chance for Western Sydney Wanderers though, nut Sharman-Lowe tips Gillion’s shot around the post.

The pitch is very, very bobbly. Excellent strike from Kavuma-McQueen for Chelsea, but Holmes tips the shot around the post.

Was that the first glimpse of “Alonso-ball”? It’s a lovely team goal, worked from back to front with some incisive passing. Terrific, powerful finish by Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old Kazakh, who joined from FC Kairat this summer. He already has nine caps for Kazakhstan.

Technically speaking, Satpayev is not officially a Chelsea player yet and is a “triallist” on this tour. He will be formally unveiled when he turns 18 in August.

The 17-year-old summer signing from Kairat Almaty has put Chelsea in front. It was a nice move from their own defensive third, drawing Western Sydney Wanderers on creating a two-on-two against their defence. Satpaev goes through and blasts a shot into the roof of the net. Good through ball from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.

Chelsea youngsters Walsh and Watson do well in midfield, and they have a free-kick on halfway. Reggie Watson is the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan Athletic midfielder Ben. A couple of stray kicks from Chelsea’s goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe. An opening for the hosts, but Hammond’s strike is wayward.

Landon Emenalo is playing at left wing-back, and he is the son of former Chelsea director of football Michael. He has had one burst forward already, and is called into some early defending to concede a throw in.

Chelsea get the game under way. The pitch looks very patchy. Incredible how clubs are willing to play mutli-million pound assets on surfaces like this.

Western Sydney Wanderers in horizontal red and black stripes, Chelsea in the season’s new blue home kit.

Off the bus. 🚎 pic.twitter.com/0sBDuEtzog

A very youthful team from the start, with some big hitters on the bench. Dastan Satpaev, 17, is a £2.1m summer signing from Kairat Almaty.

Chelsea XI: Sharman-Lowe, Acheampong, Tosin, Subuloye, Emenalo, Walsh, Watson, Essugo, Delap, Satpaev, Kavuma-McQueen

Subs: Sanchez, Curd, Palestra, Colwill, Fofana, Anselmino, Diakite, Lavia, Kellyman, Nicoll-Jazuli, Palmer, Gittens, Estevao, Joao Pedro

Chelsea started their pre-season with a 3-0 victory over Bromley in a behind-closed-doors friendly, but this morning we will have our first proper look at Xabi Alonso’s team as they take on Western Sydney Wanderers.

There was some interesting news from Stamford Bridge on Monday when it emerged the club are in talks to sign Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson. Coming after the fruitless pursuit of Granit Xhaka, the strategy suggests that Alonso has made cultural improvement a priority in a dressing room that has been accused of lacking discipline and leadership.

As ever, Chelsea have been busy in the transfer market with Morgan Rogers and Marco Palestra their headline signings, and Geovany Quenda joins up with the club from Sporting CP having been signed in March 2025.

Rogers is yet to join up with his new team-mates following his World Cup exertions with England, but fans will be looking forward to seeing how he combines with Cole Palmer.

“In that position, we needed an important player, and I’m sure that there were not many more better options than Morgan,” the 44-year-old manager told reporters. “It means a lot for everyone.”

Tasked with reviving Chelsea after a turbulent, trophyless season in which the west London club finished 10th ⁠in the Premier League, Alonso believes Rogers can combine effectively with Palmer.

“I have a plan. I have an idea. I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said of ​Rogers and Palmer, who are close ‌friends and England teammates.

“You need to have a good mix, good stability players, and players that can play with more freedom.

“And if we get that ‌balance right, ​and we get ⁠those special players in the right positions, with good control, I think that we will be more ⁠competitive with the ball ​and against the ball.”

#1731. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.

#1730. Liverpool transfer news: Brazilian heavyweights 'plot audacious swoop' for Anfield star as bitter rivals face the drop

By Seye Omidiora | 06 Nov 2026 00:28

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker has reportedly been identified as a possible target for Brazilian giants Flamengo.

The 34-year-old goalkeeper has recently entered the final 12 months of his current Anfield contract.

Liverpool activated a clause in March to extend his deal by a year, keeping him at the club until June 2027.

However, should the two parties fail to agree another extension, the veteran could leave on a free transfer next summer.

Liverpool face no immediate risk of losing their first-choice goalkeeper, but Flamengo are understood to be assessing whether a bold move is viable.

According to Sport Witness, Alisson's name has been seriously discussed by senior figures involved in Flamengo's long-term plans.

The Rio de Janeiro club are weighing up whether to make a concerted attempt to bring the experienced international back to Brazil.

Some executives feel his proven quality and elite standing would make him a strong addition to the squad.

Others are said to be more sceptical, citing his age and recent underwhelming displays for Brazil.

Flamengo are also facing financial challenges that could significantly limit their spending ahead of next season.

Even without a transfer fee, the club would need to decide whether they could meet Alisson's substantial wage demands.

Should Flamengo choose to pursue their interest, they would face a major geographical and emotional obstacle.

Alisson developed in Internacional’s academy and has previously expressed a wish to return to his boyhood club one day.

Internacional are widely considered his likeliest destination if he eventually moves back to Brazil, but they are currently fighting to avoid relegation.

According to the report, some Flamengo figures are hoping their rivals fall into the second division.

Relegation would weaken Internacional’s ability to persuade Alisson to return or meet his wage demands, potentially putting Flamengo in a stronger negotiating position.

#1729. Report: Liverpool now prepared to green light midfielder, should agree deal ASAP

Liverpool are in position otherwise green light a new midfielder deal. It really should happen as soon as possible.

Liverpool have got to sort out their midfield and they've got to do it soon. The Reds are struggling to find balance this season and while that's true for a few positions, it's particularly noticeable in the middle.

Things have reached the point where Trey Nyoni is now essentially a preferred option in midfield despite having barely played senior football ahead of this campaign. And that's after paying enormous money to sign Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai to long-term contracts.

Neither get in the starting XI as things stand. Instead, Nyoni is needed as he's essentially the only reliable holding midfielder in the squad, which goes against the very reasons for giving out those bumper contracts in the first place.

And then there's whatever's going on with Alexis Mac Allister.

Alexis Mac Allister's contract situationMac Allister made absolutely no secret of his desire to sign a new contract in the summer. He was publicly disappointed that Liverpool didn't offer him one, supposedly telling the player that they weren't in a position to do so. That's despite both Gravenberch and Szoboszlai getting deals. #1727. Opinion: European Championship winner fixes Andoni Iraola's biggest problem

Andoni Iraola has done fairly well as Liverpool's manager so far.

The Spaniard has only lost two games since being appointed as the Reds' head coach but, they're still only fifth in the Premier League table.

Their performances in the Champions League have been a sight to behold but, there are definitely still some areas among their ranks that could do with an upgrade or two.

Some players among their squad were also expected to do much better than they have done which has caused even more questions to arise.

However, fortunately for Iraola, the answer to his main problem may have just emerged.

Harvey Elliott could be on his way back to Liverpool

Liverpool have lacked creativity this season.

At the start of the campaign, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo were both in fine form and were creating chances for one another.

However, as we've gotten further into the term, things just haven't continued to work out for either of them and, others such as Florian Wirtz have failed to make a difference.

The German was expected to be the Reds' main source of creativity when he was signed by Liverpool last season but, that has been far from the case.

Despite this, the Reds have never really had any sort of cover for him so, this latest update from Football Insider about the future of Harvey Elliott is certainly intriguing.

"Liverpool intend to sell midfielder Harvey Elliott in January if Valencia terminate his loan spell, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The La Liga side are searching for a way to bring the loan deal to a premature close, with the 23-year-old still yet to start a game for them.

"There is a growing expectation that he will be sent back to Anfield in January, which sources say would effectively set him back to 'square one.'"

Harvey Elliott could become Liverpool's back-up number 10

Although Football Insider say that Liverpool want to move Elliott on, nobody is going to want to buy him without seeing how good he can be.

Most people expected him to thrive with Valencia but, once again, that's failed to happen.

Carlos Corberan was the main driving force behind the Englishman's transfer and, since he's now been sacked, it's unclear how often Elliott will be used.

The 23-year-old's time in Spain could be coming to an end and, if the Reds are wanting to make some sort of money from his sale, they need to prove his worth.

Bringing him back for the second half of the 2026-27 season would not only give Iraola another option to choose from among his ranks but would also give Wirtz a bit of a break every now and then.

He'd also fit perfectly into the Reds' plans as, right now, the main thing that they need is homegrown players.

Obviously, these are all just theories at the moment but, if Elliott is about to make his return to L4, Liverpool could certainly use him.

#1726. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#1725. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal: Resolute Gunners dig in for a big Anfield win

Fourteen years is a long time to wait for a win at any stadium, but Arsenal ensured all three points returned from Anfield to North London for the first time since 2012 yesterday.

The surprise in the team line-up was the return of Christos Tzolis who had missed a month, more or less, with a hamstring injury. If it initially felt a bit harsh on Eberechi Eze, Mikel Arteta’s post-game comments about him barely making the game because of an injury problem of his own made it make more sense.

Early on, we were really good. Plenty of the ball, playing it well in their half, and lots of control. Liverpool looked a bit off the pace, and in the opening minutes young midfielder Trey Nyoni was lucky to escape without some sanction for a nasty foul on Martin Odegaard. I think it was much more mistimed than malicious, but studs down the Achilles is never good, and we saw Crystal Palace striker Jean Philippe Mateta see red for something similar on Saturday evening.

The early pressure paid dividends when Liverpool were a little sloppy at the back. Odegaard pounced to recover the ball, it was fed to Noni Madueke via Bruno Guimaraes, and when Declan Rice overlapped, his precision ball to the back post found Kai Havertz for a tap-in to make it 1-0. That makes it 5 assists so far this season for the midfielder, all of them from open play as well, and his presence in this team reminds me so much of Patrick Vieira. Not that they’re the same kind of player, but that his importance and stature is just fundamental to us. The desire he showed with that overlap is, essentially, what cracked this game open in our favour.

There was another back post chance for Havertz, almost getting on the end of a deflected Guimaraes shot, but after that – as happens so often at Anfield – the momentum changed. This time there was no Granit Xhaka style confrontation to act as a catalyst, the game just shifted and in the final 20 minutes of the first half we rode our luck a bit.

Liverpool started to play around our box and deliver dangerous balls. One almost found Alexander Isak but a combination of David Raya and Ezri Konsa was enough to see it trickle wide. Florian Wirtz hit the bar with a free kick, and Liverpool wanted a penalty when Tzolis looked to pull back Cody Gakpo but I don’t think there was enough in that one. The next one, however, oooof.

Liverpool put in another dangerous cross, Isak was there to head towards goal from close range, and Jurrien Timber’s shirt pull absolutely prevented him from making contact with the ball. You know my rule of thumb with penalties: how would I feel it were given, or not given, up the other end, and if we didn’t get that I’d be fuming. It’s a penalty all day long, and even if the ref didn’t quite see the foul well enough, the VAR officials really ought to have suggested an on-field review. I found the focus on Isak’s reaction a bit odd. Surely the onus is on the officials to recognise what we’ve all seen without a player having to prompt them in that direction, but we got so, so lucky there.

As we did when Alexis Mac Allister ran into the box and, unmarked from 10 yards out, headed the ball over the bar when he absolutely should score. That was a very bad miss from a Liverpool perspective, and a huge chance to equalise just before the break. We needed half-time, and despite the fact Liverpool enjoyed plenty of the ball in the early part of the second period, they looked a lot less dangerous.

My explanation for this is that we leaned into one of our great strengths, which is our defensive organisation and discipline. I thought Konsa was outstanding, but so too was Riccardo Calafiori at left-back whose one on one defending has improved massively. He dealt with Gakpo, he then had to contend with Rio Ngumoha, and I just loved the concentration as he focused on the ball and more often than not prevented Liverpool from creating danger.

Myles Lewis-Skelly came on midfield, Odegaard’s pressing was relentless, and as I remarked on BlueSky afterwards, if this team could attack half as well as it can defend, we’d be the best team in the world by a mile. There were moments when we could have countered better and with more pace, but we still found some threat in the second 45. The best chance fell to Tzolis, set up by Madueke, and his first-time shot was heading for the bottom corner but for a brilliant save from Alisson.

Liverpool threw the kitchen sink at it from the bench, but it made little difference. Mac Allister then got a bit naughty, slapping Odegaard on the back of the head, then collapsing to the ground to make it look as if Madueke had leaned his head into him. Replays showed that didn’t happen, and it was pretty pathetic from the Argentina international. I guess, as well as being a risible piece of play-acting, there was an element of desperation to it, because Liverpool huffed and puffed but could not blow our house down because of how defensively outstanding we are as a team.

For the first time in Premier League history, Liverpool finished a home game without a shot on target, which tells you something. It probably tells you just how much that Timber shirt pull had an impact because a striker like Isak would at least have tested David Raya from there, but more broadly it tells you that this is a team who look laser-focused on their target this season which is to retain the title – something we’ve never done in the modern era.

Afterwards, I thought the manager’s turn of phrase was interesting when he referred to it as ‘a mission’, saying:

Just loving the mission and the mission was something that we didn’t accomplish in 14 years. You really need to enjoy that. If you don’t, there will be a moment that you will switch off and they will punish you. I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive so I’m really happy.

He’s obviously referencing winning away at Liverpool for the first time in such a long time, but I think it applies to the season as well. And, as I referenced in yesterday’s blog, there was a response to the midweek defeat to Fleetwood Town. If that was a result that as fans we could find relatively easy to compartmentalise, I don’t think the same is true for this manager because we know he wants to win every game, and it how much it stings when we don’t – especially against lower league opposition. He expected his side to deliver, saying:

It was a feeling, how the hell can that happen? How can you get out of the cup when you shoot 27 times? We had the chances that we had against a team that had put one shot on target and then you look so silly. Then you have to go to Anfield and say, how can I lift those players up? I had a feeling and I said, now is the moment. We’re going to have to dig deep, have an element of luck at times and for sure a lot of quality in the key moments and we’ve done it.

Which I think is a pretty fair assessment. We did a lot of stuff very well, we had moments of luck – which you so often need in a game like this to take all three points – but I don’t think anyone should be under any illusions that this was anything other than the champions demonstrating our title credentials again. In every season, regardless of how good you are, you need the rub of the green from time to time, like a Ruud van Nistelrooy penalty miss at Old Trafford, or Mateus Fernandes missing a huge chance for West Ham. It doesn’t change the inherent quality you possess or what you’re capable of doing, and in the cold light of day it should make you more driven to ensure you widen the margins – and by that I mean delivering a bit more in the opposition’s final third.

However, no complaints this morning. We had a job to do, and a difficult one at that, and we did exactly that to put us back on top of the table. It’s a nice place to be, but it’s still so early in the season I think we should dismiss any chat about what it means at this point. We can be impressed, but still cognisant of the fact there’s still a long, long way to go.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now, but we will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on today. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around noon or so. Until then, have a good one.

#1724. Lens vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 06 Nov 2026 00:42

Fresh off a pulverizing Champions League defeat in midweek, Lens will try to build themselves back up when they welcome Marseille to Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Sunday.

After nine matchdays, Lens sit ninth in Ligue 1, losing 1-0 at Lille last weekend, with OM now two points above them in sixth thanks to a 2-0 win over Toulouse.

Just when Lens seemed to be building some confidence, showing much more consistency domestically, that was all seemingly shattered in midweek.

With a 9-1 Champions League defeat versus Como on Wednesday, Yannick Cahuzac’s men became the first side to concede that many goals in that competition.

After Wednesday’s match, their resilience will be tested like never before, as they hope to avoid losing three successive competitive games for the first time all season.

Their European form has been messy, losing three consecutive Champions League outings by a combined margin of 14-1, though Lens have won three of their last four Ligue 1 affairs.

While they have scored just one Champions League goal at home this season, nine of their 16 domestic goals have occurred at Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

Les Sang et Or have won three of their last four Ligue 1 home meetings against Marseille, coming back to beat them 2-1 in this exact fixture last season.

While Lens are reeling following their midweek fixture, Marseille are feeling much better about their overall form of late.

Bruno Genesio’s men have won four of their last five competitive fixtures, including their first in the Europa League this season at Bayer Leverkusen on Thursday (1-0).

That was their first Europa League away win since 2023 at AEK Athens (2-0), with OM having now won three of their last four competitive games as the visitors.

On Sunday they can collect three successive competitive clean sheets for the first time in 2026, and also pick up consecutive shutouts in Ligue 1 for the first time since March.

Les Olympiens rank second in the league regarding goals per game (2.2) and average possession (55.7%), while only three points currently separate them from second-place Lille.

Marseille have scored seven goals in their last two Ligue 1 away fixtures, two more than they managed in their 10 domestic outings outside Stade Velodrome before that.

Due to adductor pain, Odsonne Edouard is doubtful for Lens, while Ismaelo Ganiou is recovering from knee surgery, Abdallah Sima has a leg issue, Jhoanner Chavez has a sore thigh and Maik Nawrocki is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Ruben Aguilar had their only goal in that embarrassing defeat to Como on Wednesday, while Florian Thauvin has three goal involvements in their last two Ligue 1 affairs at Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

As for Marseille, Derek Cornelius is dealing with a sore hip, Keyliane Abdallah has a knock and Emerson Palmieri is questionable because of a knee issue.

Amine Gouiri has goals in back-to-back competitive outings for OM, netting the winner versus Leverkusen on Thursday, while he and Amine Harit scored in their victory over Toulouse.

Risser; Aguilar, Baidoo, Antonio; Abdulhamid, Bulatovic, Cuisance, Udol; Thauvin, Sotoca; Hazard

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia, Hojbjerg, Nnadi, Abdelli; Mmadi, Gouiri, Paixao

Lens may be shell-shocked when they take to the field on Sunday after that lopsided defeat in Europe this week.

As such, we expect them to play rather timidly, which will play right into Marseille's hands, who are starting to round into form, especially in this competition.

#1723. Arsecast Extra Episode 719 – 02.11.2026

Welcome to another Arsecast Extra, the Arsenal podcast, with myself and James from @gunnerblog.

We analyse the Gunners strong start to the game, and opportunities to score a second, before the game swung back towards the home side in the last part of the first half. #1722. Opinion: Liverpool must raid Premier League rivals for £40m defender

Liverpool are currently fifth in the Premier League table.

And, while that may not seem all that bad, Arne Slot was relieved of his duties as the Reds' manager for finishing in fifth place last season.

Fortunately, Liverpool still managed to qualify for the Champions League which is a competition that they seem to be doing fairly well in.

However, it's been made more than clear from their performances against other teams such as Manchester City and Arsenal that some new additions are needed.

Without these, there's no way that they'll be able to get back to the top of the Premier League table which, at the end of the day, is going to be their main goal.

So, now that the opportunity for Liverpool to bolster their defence has emerged, it's an option that they seriously need to take.

Liverpool are interested in signing El Hadji Malick Diouf from Brentford

Recently, left-back has emerged as a big problem for Liverpool.

Both Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have failed to meet expectations with both players performing rather poorly.

Before the season properly kicked off, fans believed that midfield was going to be the main issue that the Reds would need to solve in January.

However, thanks to the recent displays put on show by the aforementioned duo, some now believe that a new left-back should be on top of their priority list.

Many different options have emerged but, recently, an update from Senegalese journalist Khadim Diakhate has linked the Reds with Brentford's El Hadji Malick Diouf.

"Transfer Market: Chelsea and Liverpool interested in El Hadji Malick Diouf after his arrival at Brentford," he wrote.

"Chelsea and Liverpool are interested in El Hadji Malick Diouf ahead of the next summer transfer window. According to our information, the two English clubs have already made contact with the agent of the Senegalese left-back.

"Having arrived at Brentford last summer, the Lion of the Teranga is already catching the eye of the Premier League's big clubs."

Liverpool must sign El Hadji Malick Diouf as their new left-back

Although Diouf may not have ended the season all that well with West Ham last term, his performances from earlier in the campaign proved that he had it in him to be an important player.

Obviously, he's still only 21 years old so there's plenty of time for him to improve but, he's already a solid left-back.

His attacking output is also fairly impressive as, whenever he gets the chance, he's always pushing up the pitch and trying to create chances.

For Iraola's system, he's literally the perfect full-back and, even though Kerkez was also seen that way, things just haven't quite clicked for the Hungarian at Liverpool this term.

Tsimikas' contract is going to expire at the end of the current season so, with no renewal yet in sight, he's going to have to be replaced soon anyway.

So, getting someone such as Diouf in during the January transfer window makes a lot of sense as it would allow him to get adjusted to life at Liverpool and to their system.

No price tag was mentioned in the tweet from Diakhate but, since the Bees spent £40 million on him in the summer, they'll at least want that back.

#1721. GdS: Milan’s €500m Adidas deal causes reaction from rivals Inter – the situation

Inter are looking enviously at their city rivals AC Milan once again after Saturday’s derby, with the news of the record Adidas deal emerging.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport on Wednesday, under the new agreement Adidas will pay Milan €50m per year for ten seasons starting from 2028-29. This is when the collaboration with PUMA ends, who currently pay €24.5m per year, as per the last accounts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The paper (via Calciomercato.com) go on to state that it is likely that the €50m yearly figure includes sporting bonuses, such as participation in the Champions League, the value of material supplies (value in kind) and a portion to be invested in promotional activities (marketing fund).

Contracts with kit makers are not limited to recognising the value of just the home, away, third and other shirts, but can extend to the sale of related products. Then, guaranteed minimums and royalties come into play that are triggered above a certain turnover threshold.

For example, in addition to the €24.5m from PUMA, €55.8m in revenues came from store, e-commerce and merchandising/licensing activities, in particular those relating to the contract with the same German company and those from licensing with Fanatics and MatchWornShirt.

As for Inter, the renewal with Nike – effective from 2023 – resulted in a 70% increase over the previous contract, but the €28m per year is not in line with the club’s current commercial value. In addition to the Milan-Adidas deal, Juventus currently get €46m per year from Adidas (€41m from 2027-28).

Inter have maintained their merchandising revenues internally, over €35m in 2025-26 thanks to the new business model introduced with Fanatics, but Nike’s €28m is too little according to the Nerazzurri’s commercial management.

The contract expires in 2031, and La Gazzetta report that they will seek to renegotiate the deal to avoid accumulating delays over the next five years. Considering that Juventus and Milan have committed to the next decade, Inter have leverage as the only one of the ‘big three’ up for grabs.

#1720. Fridges and pigs and scoring goals

We live in strange times. Sorry to start your day with this shocking revelation, I realise this is a bit of a bolt from the blue, but it’s fact. All across Europe supermarket fridges are being hacked. What a time to be alive. They used to hack, I dunno, mainframes and banks and shit, but now they’re hacking fridges.

Maybe they just got bored taking billions of made-up money from CryptoSloth and BitWomble and needed a challenge. I feel like fridges ought to be the kind of thing you just can’t hack – beyond unplugging it – but what do I know? Anyway, it’s an example of how the inter-connectivity that brings us all together every day is being weaponised and now the sliced meats in your local store are gone off because Neo pwned some large cold cupboards. As if we don’t have enough to deal with.

Such as all the people who hate the way Arsenal play. Let me be very clear, my days of caring what other people think about this football club, or pretty much anything else that’s important to me, are gone. It’s a waste of time. It’s a bit like quote that’s often attributed to George Bernard Shaw, which says ‘Never wrestle with pigs. You both get dirty and the pig likes it.’

I don’t think he actually said that, but I think we can all connect with the meaning. It applies so much to social media, and to many of the ways we’re exposed to punditry and ‘expert’ analysis in football these days. Like one of those shows where you have a couple of ex-pro pigs bleating on about this and that, and then a collection of other little pigs who support all the clubs argue with them and amongst themselves, and it’s just a pigstravaganza of pointless, inane bollocks but it does #numbers on socials so is seen as valuable #content.

I understand why opposition fans go on and on about how much they hate how Arsenal play. It’s because we win a lot of games. That’s the thing that really irks them. That’s just so basic though, you can’t appear to be clever and an aficionado of the game if you just say ‘I don’t like it when they win’, so it’s dressed up as dismissal of style or something else.

And look, here’s where the strange world we live in comes back into focus. You can, and really should, be able to hold more than one thought in your brain – about football or anything else – that holds true. I absolutely love how good we are defensively. LOVE IT. The commitment with which we are determined not to give the opposition anything is truly something to relish. Players laser-focused on their one on ones; putting bodies on the line to block shots and crosses; 11 players moving like a murmuration of birds because they’re so well drilled and organised; off the awareness and discipline; brilliantly timed tackles and headers and clearances; lads sticking up for each other when the opposition get a bit snide, as we saw on Sunday with Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke refusing to allow their captain to be treated that way; it’s all part of a brilliantly defiant defensive attitude that runs right through this team.

Creating that is not easy. As Arsenal fans we have endured defences that were porous and feeble and, at times, very, very stupid. I do not long for a return to those times. Over the years Mikel Arteta has assembled a collection of players who cannot wait to go out there and do the dirty work of defending, and it runs from front to back because that’s what he demands. If it was that easy, everyone would do it, so to castigate a team’s brilliance in one department because you just lost to them without a shot on target just comes across as sour grapes.

Here’s the other thought though. I’d really like us to be a bit better from an attacking perspective, and when I look at this team and what it’s capable of, there’s no question the forward line remains the area where you can see the room for improvement. We defend as well as we do because, more often than you or I might like, we have to – because we live through games of fine margins. A 1-0 to the Arsenal is part of our history, hard-wired into our supporter DNA (particularly if you’re of a particular vintage), but I can’t lie and wish there weren’t a few more 3-0s to the Arsenal.

I’m absolutely certain Mikel Arteta would like that too, and I think it’s a bit too easy to say that this is a team that plays precisely the football he wants it to play. He is, as we all understand, an arch pragmatist, so what we get is a team that leans into its strengths, as laid out above. He is characterised as a defensive coach, which I get, but a few seasons ago we found an attacking cocktail that drove a title challenge, and saw us score more goals that year than the Invincibles did when they won the league in 2004 (91 to 73).

I think he wants both. He wants that parsimony at the back and the firepower up front. Unfortunately, forward line recruitment is the most difficult part of transfer business, and while he as manager has a part to play in that, as a club our track record is quite poor in that regard. This summer’s window was a complete bust from an attacking perspective, not a good look when you’re pursuing players like Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez. When you then let three forwards go and add just one, there are questions to be asked of the people in charge. Arteta among them, of course, but he’s not the one whose job it is to get the deals done.

It’s why there are so many conversations around January, and what we might do. We see other clubs recruit forwards who produce on a consistent basis, while ours too often struggle to find that end product. Is it our system? Would these players find it hard to get those goals for us? Reasonable questions, but the bottom line in my opinion is that we have A+ options at the back and in midfield, while in that front three we’re a bit C-. That’s where the room for improvement is, that’s where the recruitment needs to be better (certainly better than no recruitment at all), and that’s how the games we currently win by a single goal margin, often by virtue of our defensive strength, become a bit more routine.

Simplistic? Yes. Easier said than done? Quite probably. But necessary? Absolutely. Until then though, expect more defensive masterclasses, more pig wrestling, and perhaps someone could hack our own Swedish fridge into scoring a few more goals. Worth a try!

Right, I’ll leave it there for now. I just have a small favour to ask. Arseblog has been nominated for Best Fan Media (Fran Merida) in the 2026 FSA Awards. We’re trying to retain our title, so if you could take a moment to give us a vote that would be much appreciated. You can do that here – https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/fsa-awards-2026

#1719. Le Mans vs Monaco - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 06 Nov 2026 00:47

Le Mans will hope to dig themselves out of the Ligue 1 relegation zone Sunday when they host Monaco at Stade Marie-Mavingt.

A 2-0 defeat at Troyes last week dropped MUC72 down to 17th in the table, while Monaco sit seventh after a 3-1 loss at Paris FC.

The wheels appear to have fallen off Le Mans since the season resumed after the fall international break.

Before the October window, Patrick Videira’s men had earned points in four of their first five league contests, but they will enter this weekend on a four-match winless run in this competition.

They have just one point domestically since October, which is part of the reason they sit in the final relegation spot heading into this game.

Despite their recent poor form, they are only a point below Angers and Ligue 1 safety heading into matchday 10, with only three points currently separating them from Toulouse, who are 12th.

This team have been at their best domestically at home this season, earning points in three of those four outings, scoring six of their 11 goals at Stade Marie-Mavingt.

Les Mucistes will try to avoid suffering consecutive defeats at home in the French top flight this weekend for the first time since March 2010.

The Monaco team that we saw begin this season so well have been a shadow of themselves in recent weeks domestically.

Filipe Luis has seen his side drop points in four successive Ligue 1 affairs, with the Brazilian particularly annoyed with their performance against Paris FC.

His team bounced back in midweek, defeating Nordsjaelland in the Conference League (2-0) to maintain their 100% record in that competition.

Their triumph on Thursday made Luis just the fifth Ligue 1 manager to win his first five European matches in charge of a French club and only the second this century after Peter Bosz did so at Lyon in 2021.

On Sunday, Monaco can end a two-match losing run away from home in Ligue 1, netting just once over that stretch.

Les Monegasques can stretch their competitive unbeaten run versus Le Mans to nine matches this weekend, having come away with points in their last four away games against them.

Former Monaco defender Djibril Sidibe could miss another match for Le Mans this weekend due to a foot injury, while Erwan Colas remains questionable because of a knock.

Adil Bourabaa will not be available as the central midfielder is still recovering from ankle surgery with his return likely to be sometime in early 2027.

At Monaco, Stanis Idumbo has a knock and could miss this game, and Ansu Fati remains questionable with a sore hamstring.

Folarin Balogun netted his first of the season in their loss to Paris FC, with Mathys Detourbet and Matthis Abline scoring in their Conference League triumph on Thursday, the first for the Manchester City loanee with the Principality club.

Kocik; Torrente, Yohou, Boisse; Lauray; Vercruysse, Rabillard, Bretelle, Calodat; Mafouta, Diallo

Hradecky; Vanderson, Teze, Sane, Nazinho; Camara, Zakaria; Coulibaly, Abline, Golovin; Brunner

Monaco wasted many scoring chances in their last Conference League match, but should find more clear-cut opportunities against a Le Mans side that are a little over-aggressive at the back.

#1718. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.
